description.purpose: The projection of one file space onto a disk: one directory per workspace under the owner's `base_path`, laid out from the space, a permitted program run in it, and afterwards what the program changed taken over into the workspace or kept as a proposal. THE HIVE IS THE ADDRESS -- a file space sends its projection operations to this hive path and the hive hands them on.
description.use_when: Inside a file space only (`./projection`), wherever a tool needs real files: a formatter, a generator, a test run.
description.not_in_scope: No tool menu and no path for a model (the space's callers see operations, never the directory); no watcher; no cleanup of the directory after a workspace closed; no network for a program; no write outside `base_path`.
description.contract_in: Lanes on `hop.route`: in_proj (`ws_materialize`, `ws_exec`, `ws_adopt` to `mat`; `ws_export_git`, `ws_import_git`, `ws_push`, `ws_pull` to `git`), in_answer (the space's answers to this hive's own requests, `op_id` starting `mat:` or `git:`).
description.contract_out: Routes on `hop.route`, leaving through the hive path: answer (one per in_proj request, `op`, `op_id`, `caller` mirrored), in_ws / in_read / in_write (requests to the file space with `caller` 'projection').

accepts.because: a projection operation: body `{op, args}`, hop `op`, `op_id`, `ws` (a workspace name or id), `caller?`. `ws_materialize(force?)`, `ws_exec(argv, timeout_ms?)`, `ws_adopt(run, ids | 'all')` (cell `mat`); `ws_export_git(note)`, `ws_import_git(source, ref?)`, `ws_push(remote, branch?)`, `ws_pull(remote, branch?)` (cell `git`, GH #906). Answered by exactly one `answer`
the file space's answer to one of this hive's requests, `op_id` `mat:<job>:<n>` (to `mat`) or `git:<job>.<n>` (to `git`); never answered

emits.because: exactly one per in_proj request, hop `op`, `op_id`, `caller` unchanged: `{ok, op, op_id, ws, ...}` or `{ok: false, op, op_id, error: {code, message}}`
`ws_tree` of the workspace, `caller` 'projection', `op_id` `mat:<job>:t` (`git` asks it too, `git:<job>.<n>`: an import compares against it, an export learns the root)
`raw` of one version to lay it out, `caller` 'projection', hop `ws` the workspace name

what a run changed, taken over: `overwrite` against the laid-out version, `create`, `remove`, each with hop `ws` the workspace name and `caller` 'projection'; `git` writes an import the same way, one file per step
